title: Commissioners' Meeting 09/22/25
tldr: The Board adopted an ordinance limiting motorized vehicles, aircraft (including motorized paragliders), bicycles and watercraft on County property to designated areas, after a public hearing prompted by complaints about paraglider use of the Gallimore Road park. It reallocated remaining Dogwood housing infrastructure grant funds to Habitat for Humanity, Housing Assistance Corporation and engineering for Brevard's Azalea/Rhododendron sewer project. From the County's $10 million State allocation it committed $3.8 million to the Town of Rosman (contingent on an MOU) and $1.3 million to the Pisgah Labs sewer extension, and it tabled other municipal requests. The Board also endorsed a $62 million needs-based school capital grant application with language limiting its support to this application, approved revised Transylvania Natural Resources Council bylaws 4-1 with Commissioner Dalton opposed amid extensive public comment against the TNRC changes, and marked the one-year anniversary of Hurricane Helene with a resolution and recovery update.

keyVotes.description: Approve the consent agenda, including the Blue Ridge Rising resolution, opioid settlement participation and a $297,000 Gallimore Road/Boys and Girls Club sewer contract
keyVotes.background: The consent agenda included sealed May 12 closed session minutes; the August 2025 tax discovery, release and settlement report (releases $33,752.41, refunds $1,291.87); donation of surplus Library picnic tables to Connestee Fire Rescue (Resolution #39-2025); a resolution supporting Blue Ridge Parkway repair funding and the Blue Ridge Rising plan (Resolution #40-2025); a resolution joining the Purdue Pharma/Sackler and secondary opioid manufacturer settlements and SAAF-3 (County maximum of $615,236.96 and $98,322); the County Manager's $1,600 out-of-state travel to the ICMA conference; an amendment extending the FY 2024 audit contract with Martin Starnes & Associates to October 31, 2025; and award of the Gallimore Road/Boys and Girls Club sewer contract to T.P. Howard's Plumbing Co. for $297,000 (Resolution #41-2025).
keyVotes.discussion: On the Blue Ridge Rising item, Commissioner McCall emphasized the Parkway's role in tourism and local economies and the importance of repair funding after Hurricane Helene, noting her 37-year career with the Blue Ridge Parkway.

keyVotes.description: Adopt resolution in remembrance of the one-year anniversary of Hurricane Helene
keyVotes.background: Budget and Management Analyst Jennifer Wright presented a remembrance and launched the County's Hurricane Helene Retrospective Project, a series of short staff interview videos. Resolution #37-2025 recognizes September 27, 2025 as the one-year anniversary and thanks those who responded.
keyVotes.discussion: Commissioners offered reflections: Chapman noted over 130 lives lost and an estimated $62 billion in statewide damage; McCall praised the Incident Command Team; Dalton recognized Senator Corbin's help securing emergency mobile towers; McKelvey reflected on unity among staff and residents; Chairman Chappell emphasized teamwork and acknowledged Senator Corbin, Representative Clampitt and Congressman Edwards.

keyVotes.description: Reallocate remaining Dogwood grant funds to Habitat for Humanity (49 units), Housing Assistance Corporation ($440,000) and Azalea Avenue engineering and permitting (up to $662,500)
keyVotes.background: The County Manager reported that the original deliverables of the County's $2 million Dogwood ARPA Advantage Housing Infrastructure Grant were complete or nearly complete, with about $1.8 million remaining and a December deadline. She recommended fully funding the $636,000 Habitat for Humanity project with a 49-unit, two-year outcome, funding the Housing Assistance Corporation project at $440,000 with a 20-unit, two-year outcome, and applying any remaining balance up to $662,500 to engineering and permitting for the City of Brevard's Azalea/Rhododendron project.
keyVotes.discussion: Chairman Chappell asked about the reallocation process. Commissioner Chapman asked whether the projects would meaningfully affect housing needs and serve teachers and law enforcement; the Manager said the Habitat and HAC projects would add roughly 70 units targeting households at 80% AMI and below. Commissioner Dalton asked whether the Azalea funding would support new development or failing septic systems. City Manager Wilson Hooper explained the City's proposed annexation waivers tied to deed restrictions, and Commissioners McCall and McKelvey expressed concerns about deed restrictions and property rights.

keyVotes.description: Allocate $3.8 million to the Town of Rosman from the County's $10 million State allocation, contingent on an MOU
keyVotes.background: About $8.7 million of the County's $10 million 2023 State infrastructure allocation remained available. Rosman's unfunded requests totaled $24 million, including wastewater retrofits and a water treatment plant; the allocation is contingent on a Memorandum of Understanding to support future maintenance and expansion.
keyVotes.discussion: The Manager noted the Rosman project would not generate new revenue and asked for guidance on MOU terms, such as whether Rosman should set aside existing revenue for maintenance, offering to provide draft options. Chairman Chappell suggested establishing a timeframe for a response. Commissioners McCall and Dalton earlier expressed disappointment that no Rosman representatives attended.

keyVotes.description: Allocate $1.3 million for the Pisgah Labs sewer extension from the County's $10 million State allocation, returning $800,000 to unassigned fund balance
keyVotes.background: The County had pledged up to $800,000 from fund balance as a match for the City of Brevard's EDA grant to extend water and sewer to Pisgah Labs, and engineering estimates indicated an additional $500,000 would likely be needed. The Manager recommended funding the full $1.3 million from the State allocation to preserve fund balance and avoid risk of losing unspent State funds.
keyVotes.discussion: Commissioner Dalton confirmed the purpose was to shift the project's funding from fund balance to the State allocation; the Manager explained the $800,000 was recorded as assigned fund balance and would return to unassigned fund balance.

keyVotes.description: Adopt ordinance regulating vehicles, bicycles, aircraft and watercraft on County-owned property, with direction to research higher fines
keyVotes.background: Neighbors of the Gallimore Road park complained about a company using the property for motorized paraglider takeoffs and landings. The ordinance limits such use to designated areas, exempts public purpose use, allows Board-granted special permission with a fee and proof of insurance, and sets civil penalties; it could be adopted at this meeting only with a unanimous vote.
keyVotes.discussion: Chairman Chappell summarized hearing comments and noted recent State law limits local criminal penalties. Commissioner Chapman said changing the penalty type would not be a significant deterrent. Commissioner McCall asked whether the $50 civil fine could be increased, and Commissioner McKelvey suggested tiered fines for repeat offenses. The Manager said she can issue temporary trespass orders, signs would be posted starting at Gallimore Road, and an NCACC intern is researching broader park rules.

keyVotes.description: Endorse Needs-Based Public School Capital Fund grant application requesting $62 million, with a statement limiting support to this application
keyVotes.background: The application, endorsed by the Board of Education on September 15 and due October 3, seeks funding to consolidate Davidson River Alternative School onto the Brevard High School campus and build a new 70,000 sq. ft. CTE facility at Brevard High. It requests the $62 million maximum with a required $9.3 million County match; Superintendent Dr. Lisa Fletcher answered questions.
keyVotes.discussion: Commissioner Chapman asked about match sources, the future of the Davidson River building and opportunities for Rosman students. Commissioner McCall asked whether the Davidson River building is historic. Commissioner McKelvey raised concerns about long-term consolidation pressure on Rosman High School, and Chairman Chappell proposed added language stating the Board's support is only for this application and implies no support for other consolidation. Commissioner Dalton noted Rosman High's CTE facilities were upgraded in 2011.

keyVotes.description: Approve four-month Environmental Health Supervisor overlap (about $2,960) using budgeted funds
keyVotes.background: Public Health Director Elaine Russell presented the request ahead of Environmental Health Supervisor Jim Boyer's retirement effective January 31, 2026. Neill Cagle was selected as successor, and an October-January overlap costing about $2,960 would be covered by salary savings.
keyVotes.discussion: Chairman Chappell emphasized the importance of overlap to prevent disruptions across critical services.

keyVotes.description: Approve revised Transylvania Natural Resources Council bylaws, adding an ex officio County Commissioner
keyVotes.background: Following the Board's September 8 direction to reorganize the TNRC, the revised bylaws narrow its role to advising the Planning Board on environmental regulatory ordinances, replace quarterly meetings with meetings as needed plus one annual organizational meeting, and remove annual reporting. Membership remains at 15.
keyVotes.discussion: Chairman Chappell said citizen advisory councils are a resource to the Board and valued partner agencies' expertise. Commissioner Chapman stressed that boards should be productive and aligned with County priorities. Commissioner Dalton suggested appointing a Commissioner to improve communication, supported the ex officio option, said he supported the current TNRC structure, and volunteered to serve. Commissioner McCall said the reorganization was part of efficiency efforts and the process was conducted in open session.

topics.text: Said he had received numerous citizen complaints about paraglider noise and nuisance and supported moving forward with the County property ordinance.
Said he did not view changing the ordinance penalty from civil to criminal as a significant deterrent.
Noted Helene caused over 130 deaths and an estimated $62 billion in statewide damage and commended staff, responders and community organizations.
Praised Congressman Edwards and his staff for their engagement and accessibility during the Helene response.
Asked whether school construction had caused significant classroom disruptions.
Asked when groundbreaking on the new courthouse is anticipated.
Asked whether the proposed housing infrastructure projects would meaningfully affect local housing needs and whether they would serve law enforcement officers and teachers.
Asked about the City of Brevard's wastewater capacity to support the projects.

Said funding priorities should favor projects that also leverage economic development, such as buying capacity from Brevard or extending lines, and noted annexation requirements have challenged some developers.
Asked whether Azalea/Rhododendron homeowners would be required to connect to new utilities.
Asked about decision timelines for the infrastructure funds.

Asked whether the $9.3 million school grant match would come from fund balance, whether the Davidson River Alternative School building would be closed or repurposed, and whether the new CTE facility would benefit Rosman students.
Expressed strong support for the needs-based school grant application, saying the consolidation element could improve competitiveness.
Emphasized that advisory boards should be productive and aligned with County priorities and acknowledged David Whitmire's interim service as TNRC chair.
Supported adding a Commissioner to the TNRC as a non-voting ex officio member.
Shared NCACC Map Book statistics, including a median age of 52, 15.5% of residents under 18 and the 14th lowest property tax rate, and noted property valuations are governed by State rules.
Encouraged residents concerned about the TNRC to attend its meetings or review its minutes and said the TNRC remains a viable committee open to project ideas.
Described attending a naturalization ceremony and said he hopes to discuss citizenship education in local schools with Dr. Fletcher.
Noted that the young woman murdered on a Charlotte train was a friend of his granddaughter.
Recognized the County's resourcefulness during the Helene communication outage and Senator Corbin's help securing emergency mobile towers.
Noted Avery County had used its entire $60 million budget as collateral for cleanup and expressed gratitude Transylvania did not have to.
Said County representatives were vocal in criticizing the federal and State debris assistance process and that the criticism was not well received.
Said closing out Tropical Storm Fred reimbursements shortly before Helene helped staff, and called the multi-contractor debris removal process inefficient.
Asked whether inaccurate 2018 storm line data may be contributing to a sinking corner at the Rosman High School old gym.
Noted multiple small seismic events in that part of the County this year could affect infrastructure over time.
Asked whether Azalea/Rhododendron funding would support new development or address failing septic systems.
Confirmed the proposal to move Pisgah Labs extension funding from fund balance to the State allocation.
Asked whether the City of Brevard had pursued Hurricane Helene recovery funding for its projects.
Supported the three Dogwood projects and exploring Rosman wastewater upgrades to support Gaia Herbs, and suggested seeking Helene funds for generators at the Town's wells.
Expressed disappointment that no Town of Rosman representatives attended to present their projects.
Said managing the allocations was a positive problem reflecting the County's success in securing funding.
Consulted with Senator Corbin, together with Chairman Chappell, who confirmed school grant awards do not affect future eligibility.
Said Rosman High's CTE facilities, upgraded in 2011, remain capable of supporting programs like welding and agriculture.
Asked about the expected timeline for the school grant decision.
Suggested appointing a Commissioner to the TNRC, supported the ex officio option, said he supported the current TNRC structure, acknowledged David Whitmire's service, and volunteered to serve.
Congratulated the Town of Rosman on a more than $300,000 PARTF grant for Champion Park and noted the Constitution Week kickoff.
Emphasized the Blue Ridge Parkway's role in tourism and local economies and the need for Helene repair funding, noting her 37-year career with the Parkway.
Praised the professionalism and endurance of the County's Incident Command Team during Helene.
Asked when information would be available on whether the Rosman retaining wall scope needs revision.
Asked whether projected interest rate cuts would affect courthouse financing.

Asked whether the City Attorney had reviewed the City's proposed deed restrictions and expressed concern that they could limit owners' ability to sell at market value and allow utility service termination.
Asked whether $8.5 million would complete Phase 1 of Brevard's wastewater plant upgrade and whether the plant is at capacity.

Favored letting Brevard and Rosman submit highest-priority proposals and said the County has limited capacity to fund all projects without raising taxes, encouraging the municipalities to use their own taxing authority.
Asked whether an agreement was in place for pretreatment of leachate associated with the Gaia Herbs project.

Said funding approvals should be contingent on agreements, supported $3.8 million for Rosman with an agreement, and was willing to consider $1.8 million for Azalea Avenue contingent on final deed restrictions.
Asked to table the remaining infrastructure requests pending deed restriction language and priority proposals from Brevard and Rosman, and stressed the importance of Rosman representatives attending.
Asked whether the $50 civil fine in the vehicle ordinance was appropriate and could be increased.
Asked whether the Davidson River Alternative School building is historic and noted designation could restrict remodeling while valuing preservation.
Noted that if the school grant is approved, the scope of some current projects may need adjustment.
Highlighted the age of school facilities and encouraged the Board of Education to develop a long-term facilities strategic plan.
Supported adding an ex officio Commissioner to the TNRC, said the reorganization is part of efficiency efforts, and said the bylaws process was conducted in open, publicly noticed meetings.
Offered prayers for victims of recent national and State tragedies.
Reflected on the unity and compassion shown by staff and residents during Helene.
Asked when the City Council would finalize deed restriction language and what would happen if an owner did not comply.

Confirmed that the $5.5 million Azalea/Rhododendron project would provide utility access to all parcels with failing septic systems, and that a $1.8 million County contribution would leave roughly $4 million.
Supported acting separately on the $3.8 million Rosman allocation and making remaining allocations contingent on the City's deed language.
Suggested considering tiered fines for repeat offenses under the vehicle ordinance.
Thanked Dr. Fletcher but voiced concern that a large CTE facility at Brevard High could shift consolidation pressure onto Rosman High, and asked for language protecting Rosman's identity and voice.
Emphasized teamwork among County departments, emergency services, churches and partners during Helene and acknowledged Senator Corbin, Representative Clampitt and Congressman Edwards.
Called the disaster assistance process confusing and frustrating, recounting that counties were assigned to handle applications without eligibility information despite County objections.
Commended staff for a conservative approach to disaster funds that he said left the County in a stronger fiscal position than many neighbors.
Said several Commissioners recently met with General Assembly members, including Senator Corbin, to seek State support for major projects such as the courthouse.
Asked whether the Dogwood reallocation required formal Board action.
Suggested setting a timeframe for Rosman's response on the MOU.
Noted recent State law limits local authority to impose criminal penalties and that most concern stemmed from an out-of-county motorized paragliding company.
Asked whether the school grant match must be spent on the specific areas in the application.
Proposed language stating the Board's support covers only this grant application and implies no support for additional school consolidation.
Noted the needs-based grant is now administered by the Treasurer's Office rather than NCDPI.
Emphasized the importance of the Environmental Health supervisor overlap to prevent service disruptions.
Said citizen advisory councils are a resource to the Board, expressed appreciation for TNRC partner agencies, and noted the ex officio appointment could rotate among Commissioners.

publicComments.speaker: Alan Mercaldo
publicComments.summary: Supported the motorized vehicle ordinance and suggested removing language that could cause confusion about overlapping State and local rules, clarifying that special permits are not automatic, and considering criminal rather than civil penalties enforced by the Sheriff.

publicComments.speaker: Nicholas Holshouser
publicComments.summary: Supported the ordinance, saying motorized aircraft present safety and nuisance issues at the park, which was once an airfield, and urged adoption.

publicComments.speaker: Owen Carson
publicComments.summary: As outgoing TNRC chair, objected to the Board's reorganization of the TNRC and limits on its opportunity to speak, described its value for interagency coordination and public education, and asked what prompted the change.

publicComments.speaker: Annette Raines
publicComments.summary: Distributed a handout on single-wide mobile home valuations and urged the Board to use the additional 30-day review period for appeals to address valuation concerns.

publicComments.speaker: David Whitmire
publicComments.summary: Supported Mr. Carson, clarified how TNRC minutes and presentations were handled, and encouraged the Board to use its influence with resource managers to support responsible forest management.

publicComments.speaker: Clare Hannon
publicComments.summary: Described repeated attempts to obtain Helene debris removal assistance for her property, which remains uncleared, and raised safety concerns given a nearby wildfire.

publicComments.speaker: Alice Wellborn
publicComments.summary: Agreed public employees should not face abuse but said Commissioners' own conduct toward one another and the public often falls short, and urged them to model civility.

publicComments.speaker: Margie Huggins
publicComments.summary: Reported vandalism releasing water from the Cascade Lake Dam that harmed aquatic habitats and urged the Board to reconsider maintaining the TNRC.

publicComments.speaker: Owen Carson
publicComments.summary: In the second comment period, said Board members had mischaracterized the TNRC, cited its work on flooding, debris and wildfire preparedness, and called for more transparency and collaboration.

publicComments.speaker: Lee McMinn
publicComments.summary: A former six-year TNRC chair, said the action effectively demoted the TNRC to an ad hoc committee, questioned how partner agencies would respond, and noted past recommendations such as a higher base flood elevation standard were not acted on.

publicComments.speaker: Heath Cartee
publicComments.summary: Described the local connection to land and water and urged Commissioners to act as caretakers and consider the long-term impact of decisions such as those on the TNRC.

publicComments.speaker: Jenny Cartee
publicComments.summary: Called the Board's TNRC actions inconsiderate to a 20-year volunteer group, stressed its role linking the County, forest managers and the public, and said the Board appears to discourage an engaged public.

publicComments.speaker: Peter Offen
publicComments.summary: Said the TNRC is important for resource preservation and community safety, criticized the Board's ecological expertise and planning, and reminded the Board that City residents are also County taxpayers.

publicComments.speaker: Margie Huggins
publicComments.summary: Encouraged a plan allowing the TNRC to keep meeting, suggested a project-based approach with educational and hands-on projects, and asked the Board to consider monthly meetings or structured proposals.

publicComments.speaker: Clare Hannon
publicComments.summary: Acknowledged volunteers who helped neighbors after Helene and noted the meeting coincided with the start of Rosh Hashanah, highlighting inclusivity.

publicComments.speaker: Hannah Bowers
publicComments.summary: Said many County employees praised for Helene work are not paid a living wage, noting some essential service positions start at $12.54 per hour.

publicComments.speaker: Aaron Baker
publicComments.summary: A Brevard City Councilman, described failing septic systems in the Azalea/Rhododendron neighborhood and urged City-County cooperation to provide water and sewer.

followUps.description: Research the potential for higher fines under the new County property vehicle ordinance after confirming statutory limits.
Post signs under the new vehicle ordinance, beginning with the Gallimore Road park property.
Complete research by the NCACC intern on broader County park rules and bring it back for future review.
Submit the Dogwood grant reallocation request, confirm details with Dogwood, and update the Board once Dogwood responds and coordination with the City is complete.
Draft MOU options and agreements for the $3.8 million Rosman allocation and the Pisgah Labs extension for Board consideration at the next meeting.
followUps.resolution: The Board approved the terms of the infrastructure funding MOU to offer to the Town of Rosman. The Pisgah Labs extension was not addressed in these minutes.

followUps.description: Send formal requests to the City of Brevard and Town of Rosman for their highest-priority project proposals and notify them of the remaining balance of the $10 million State allocation.
Request the Town of Rosman's preliminary engineering report for its State-funded projects to give the Board more detail.
Request that Town of Rosman representatives attend future discussions, and explore a possible joint meeting with the City and Town.
Insert the ex officio County Commissioner language into Article III.B of the revised TNRC bylaws.
Present the 10-year population and enrollment study, expected in February, to support facilities planning.

(minutes: "The Board could also consider limited agreements linking County funding to specific benefits, similar to the prior City-County agreement or a past revenue-sharing proposal with the Town of Rosman." (p. 21))
